title: Giving Advice
summary: A friend asks for advice about moving to a new city for a job and gets practical suggestions.
description: An intermediate conversation focused on advice structures ('You should…', 'Why don't you…', 'Have you thought about…?'). The dialogue models a friendly, supportive tone.

vocabulary.definition: an opinion you give someone about what they should do
to mention an idea or plan that someone might consider
to think carefully about something before deciding
to have enough money to pay for something
money you pay to use a room, flat or house that belongs to someone else

dialogue.text: I need some advice, Mark. I am thinking about moving to Edinburgh for a new job.
That sounds exciting. Have you considered the cost of living there?
Not really. Rents are higher than in my city, but I think I can afford it.
Good. You should also look for a flat near public transport. Traffic can be heavy.
That is a good idea. What about meeting new people?
Why don't you join a club or a class? It is the easiest way to make friends.
I never thought about that. Any other suggestions?
Yes. Save money for the first three months. Moving is always more expensive than you expect.
Thanks, Mark. I feel much better about the decision now.

questions.q: Why is the speaker thinking about moving?
What does Mark suggest about transport?
What is one suggestion for meeting people?

trueFalse.statement: Mark says Edinburgh is more expensive than the speaker's city.
trueFalse.explanation: Mark says 'Rents are higher than in my city,' which the speaker accepts.

trueFalse.statement: Mark recommends spending all the savings before moving.
trueFalse.explanation: Mark says the opposite: 'Save money for the first three months.'

teacherTips: Drill the three advice structures from the dialogue: 'You should…', 'Why don't you…?', 'Have you considered…?'
After listening, learners ask each other for advice on a real-life decision using the same structures.
Optional writing follow-up: a short paragraph giving advice to a friend who is moving abroad.

es.title: Dar consejo
es.summary: Un amigo pide consejo sobre mudarse a una nueva ciudad por trabajo y recibe sugerencias prácticas.
es.description: Una conversación intermedia centrada en estructuras de consejo ('You should…', 'Why don't you…', 'Have you thought about…?'). El diálogo modela un tono amable y de apoyo.

vocabulary.definition: una opinión que le das a alguien sobre lo que debería hacer
mencionar una idea o plan que alguien podría considerar
pensar cuidadosamente sobre algo antes de decidir
tener suficiente dinero para pagar algo
dinero que pagas por usar una habitación, piso o casa que pertenece a otra persona

questions.q: ¿Por qué está pensando en mudarse el interlocutor?
¿Cuál es una sugerencia para conocer gente?

trueFalse.statement: Mark dice que Edimburgo es más caro que la ciudad del interlocutor.
trueFalse.explanation: Mark dice 'Rents are higher than in my city', y el interlocutor lo acepta.

trueFalse.statement: Mark recomienda gastarse todos los ahorros antes de mudarse.
trueFalse.explanation: Mark dice lo contrario: 'Save money for the first three months'.

teacherTips: Practica las tres estructuras de consejo del diálogo: 'You should…', 'Why don't you…?', 'Have you considered…?'.
Después de escuchar, los estudiantes se piden consejo mutuamente sobre una decisión de la vida real usando las mismas estructuras.
Ampliación opcional de escritura: un párrafo corto dando consejo a un amigo que se muda al extranjero.
